title: Task classification and gate policy
description: The contract read by bin/ai-task-gates. The central file is config/task-gates.json in popcre/ai-devops. A consumer repository ships a much smaller file of the same shape at .ai-devops/task-gates.json, carrying only `paths` and `gates`. Resolution takes the STRONGEST class per path across the central default, every matching central rule, and the consumer declaration, so a consumer can only strengthen a class and can never weaken one.

_comment.description: Free prose for the humans reading the file. Ignored by the tool.

actions.description: Every action a session can ask permission for. Central file only; an action name used anywhere else must appear here.

change_classes.description: What a change can be. Central file only. `rank` orders strength and the strongest matching class always wins; a `protected` class can never be acknowledged or owner-requested away.

default.description: The baseline applied to every repository, before its own central rules and its own declaration.

fallback_class.description: The class for a changed path that matches no glob. It must never be the weakest class, or an unrecognised file would quietly downgrade the task.

rules.description: Per-repository additions to the baseline. EVERY rule whose `match` matches applies; matching is additive, never exclusive.

match.description: Shell glob matched against the canonical owner/repo identity, for example */designflow-*.

paths.description: Consumer declaration only: the repository's own path rules, added on top of everything central.

gates.description: Consumer declaration only: extra required proofs and forbidden actions, unioned with the central gate for the same class.

pathRules.description: Ordered list mapping a changed path to the class it implies. Order does not decide the outcome — the strongest matching class does.

glob.description: Shell glob matched against a repository-relative changed path, for example db/migrations/**.

gateTable.description: Which gates apply to a class, kept deliberately separate from which class a path implies.

required.description: Proofs that must exist before this class of work may ship.

forbidden_actions.description: Action names this class refuses. A refusal for a protected class is final.
